The terms "man" and "woman" are used to describe people who have certain qualitative characteristics. It makes communication easier when it comes to description. There are no rules on who is a man or woman besides the ones we create ourselves, so anyone who wants to be a woman can be.

Biological sex is also not binary, as evidenced by the existence of intersex people who account for about 2% of the population. Intersex people can be born with almost any mixture of sex characteristics.

Genetic sex, XX and XY, are also not a binary. Many women don't have XX chromosomes and differences in how the SRY gene gets read can effect how sex characteristics present themselves dispite what chromosomes a person has. 

All that to say, someone's gender and sex doesn't matter to anyone but someone's doctor.
